cands.bio: Monroeville-area Republican who has twice run for Alabama House District 68. Longtime marketing and safety director at South Alabama Gas, master pipe fitter, commercial pilot, and former owner of radio station WYNI. Chaplain for the Monroe County Sheriff's Department and a foster parent. He has never held public office.

endorsements.text: His campaign site lists Nathaniel Ledbetter, Speaker of the Alabama House of Representatives, as an endorser, with a quote saying Kelley would represent his district conservatively on moral issues.
His campaign site lists Rev. Greg Davis, President and CEO of the Alabama Citizens Action Program (ALCAP), as an endorser.

cands.gaps: Kelley has never held office, so there is no legislative record to review. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, school choice or teacher pay, or policing. His campaign site says only "lower taxes" and "strengthening our schools" in general terms. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and the position statements we have come from his 2022 survey and his campaign site. We found no independent reporting or official records confirming his radio station ownership or his endorsements.

qual.background: He worked about 30 years at South Alabama Gas as marketing and safety director, worked as a master pipe fitter, and by his campaign's account owned and operated radio station WYNI in Monroeville. He has held no elected office and lost the 2022 and 2026 races for this seat.
qual.why: He has business ownership and management experience but no legislative, policy or budget work and no prior elected office, which puts him in the middle range. Board service, chaplain work and volunteer roles were not counted.

second-amendment.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he believes in the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms and in "Constitutional Carry."

pro-life.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he believes in the rights of the unborn child.
